name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.199.0 — Mock contract moves to version 3 — design/decisions.json and approval.theme are retired, per-screen approval is recorded by mock-review approve --screen <name> run by the session rather than by a control on the served page, and the mocks driver's client waive now calls the package's waive verb so no script in this repo writes a design document. 7.198.0 — The mock stage's theme step no longer tells the session to pick a theme on the served page — that control does not exist under ADR-0029's actor model; the person running the stage sets theme: "<k>" in mock.config.ts from the back. § Provenance Ledger's exclusion-row note grammar gains the deferred: <id> form the same section's own rewritten first sentence, and --mark approved itself, already write. 7.197.0 — The mocks stage's seed grammar becomes numbered client-sentence beats ("sentence" -> screen[@state]), copied verbatim into src/journeys.ts and proven by check --json rather than a names-and-arrows surfaces block; the reviewer contract bumps to v2 to carry step.beat and the narrowed approval.journeys{} shape. The CLIENT state collapses — the client now walks the served app during SCREENS and confirms each journey against a hash of its own beats, the one human gate left in the stage — and a note's fourth status, deferred, lands as a ledger exclusion row at --mark approved instead of the retired ledger derive.
